To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) low BW is related to rise of pulse pressure among adult obese subjects; (ii) such relationship is independent from any other correlate of metabolic syndrome; (iii) the effect is more pronounced among men; (iv) the effect is independent from any weight gain in adulthood; (v) the effect is not due to the presence of overweight-obese status.
low birth-weight is related to rise of pulse pressure in adult overweight-obesity, independently of other correlates of metabolic syndromes.
in overweight-obese people, low birth weight is inversely associated with pulse pressure, independently from other correlates of the metabolic syndrome.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the relationship between birth weight and blood pressure in a sample of adult, apparently healthy, overweight-obese individuals and the effect that overweight and/or obesity might have on this relationship.
the relationship between low birth weight and pulse pressure among overweight-obese subjects.

the hypothesis of whether low birth-weight is associated with a rise in blood pressure later in life and whether presence of overweight or obesity modifies this relationship, independent of other metabolic correlates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
low BW is a risk factor for rise of BP in adulthood, but such risk is more relevant in men than in women, in the absence of overweight-obesity.
low birth weight is related to a higher risk of elevated pulse pressure in adulthood only in the presence of overweight-obese status, in men.
low BW is associated with rise in BP in adult overweight-obesity, and that this relationship is independent of other metabolic correlates, but is more evident among males.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lower the BW the higher the risk of having elevated PP, independently from other risk factors of metabolic syndrome.
the lower the birth weight the higher the risk of developing vascular damage in adulthood, especially if overweight-obese.
low birth weight is a risk factor for rise of pulse pressure in adult overweight-obesity, independently of other correlates of metabolic syndromes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
low birth weight is a risk factor for rise of pulse pressure in overweight-obese adults.
low birth-weight is a relevant factor for the development of vascular damage among overweight-obese people.
low birth-weight (BW, below 2,500 g) is associated with rise in pulse pressure (PP) later in life, uniquely in men and independently from other correlates of cardiovascular risk.
